title: Redundant Derived Fields Requiring Manual Synchronization
pattern: A struct stores both primary inputs and a deterministically derived value as independent state, requiring updates to be kept synchronized.
why_bad: Updating a source field without its derivative violates the single source of truth and leaves internally inconsistent state that can silently affect later behavior.
detection: Identify a field computed entirely from other fields in the same struct, such as diameter from rim/tire or length from endpoints. Inspect mutation paths to determine whether storing the derivative creates independent synchronization obligations rather than a justified, coherently maintained cache.
counterexample: Caching an expensive computation for a demonstrated performance requirement when mutation and cache invalidation/recomputation are encapsulated (e.g., via interior mutability) so the cached value remains coherent. Expense alone does not excuse stale values.
source: Sandi Metz, *Practical Object-Oriented Design* (2019), Chapter 2 ("Designing Classes with a Single Responsibility"), pp. 177-178; *The Pragmatic Programmer* (20th Anniversary Edition), Topic 9: "DRY—The Evils of Duplication", p. 202-203.
